question: What is Walmart's total debt (short and long term, including finance leases) and its net debt or net cash, and how are interest expense and interest coverage trending?

answer.summary: Walmart's total debt (short and long term, including finance leases) was $37.01B as of January 31, 2024, up 5.7% YoY from $35.02B at January 31, 2023 [F01863][F01862]. Long-term debt comprised the bulk at $36.13B (up 4.3% YoY) [F00137], while short-term borrowings rose sharply from $372.00M to $878.00M (+136.0% YoY) [F00121][F00122]. Net debt was positive at $27.14B as of FY2024, up 2.8% YoY from $26.40B [F01865][F01864], so the company carries net debt rather than net cash. Cash and cash equivalents grew 14.4% YoY to $9.87B [F00099], which partially offset the debt increase. Debt-to-equity declined modestly to 0.44x from 0.46x (-3.4% YoY) [F01867][F01866]. Interest expense and interest coverage figures are not in the retrieved evidence; only the weighted-average interest rate on short-term borrowings (7.7% in FY2024 vs 6.6% in FY2023) is disclosed [T00510].
drivers: Total debt +5.7% YoY driven primarily by long-term debt +4.3% YoY ($34.65B -> $36.13B) [F00137], with short-term borrowings as a smaller but rapidly growing component (+136.0% YoY) [F00121].
Net debt +2.8% YoY ($26.40B -> $27.14B) [F01865] reflects debt growth outpacing cash growth; cash +14.4% YoY to $9.87B [F00099] partially offset the debt increase.
Debt-to-equity -3.4% YoY (0.46x -> 0.44x) [F01867] indicates leverage ratio improved slightly despite higher absolute debt, as equity grew faster than debt.
risks_and_red_flags: Short-term borrowings more than doubled (+136.0% YoY) from $372.00M to $878.00M [F00121][F00122], a strong increase that warrants monitoring of near-term refinancing needs.
Net debt remains positive at $27.14B [F01865]; the company does not hold net cash, so interest costs remain a real burden.
